name: Make-Up
label: Dischord
lede: Nation of Ulysses called itself a political party. Its successor ran like a church: matching suits, a congregation instead of an audience, and a five-year plan to quit once everybody started copying them.

eras.title: From party to congregation
eras.text: Nation of Ulysses ended in 1992. Ian Svenonius, James Canty and Steve Gamboa started over with bassist Michelle Mae, up from Olympia, and traded the manifesto for the shape of a gospel service: call, response, and the audience as a fifth member.

years.h: Before Make-Up, there's Cupid Car Club, M.P.
years.p: Svenonius, Canty and Gamboa play together in the short-lived Cupid Car Club, M.P. It leaves one 7", Werewolves, on Kill Rock Stars.

years.cap: The four members in front of a shuttered storefront, 1997
q: Our music is gospel-based. It's rhythm-based, with a subverted guitar.
years.h: Make-Up opens in February 1995, dressed alike
years.p: Svenonius sings, Canty plays guitar and organ, Gamboa moves from bass to drums, and Mae joins on bass from Olympia's [[The Frumpies|02231403-76b1-4a4c-accc-714eda94566f]].
years.xp:
Dischord dates the start to February 1995 and describes a group with the "freneticism, catharsis and spirituality" of gospel, a "total departure from the boring pantomime of rock 'n' roll." The sound had its own name, gospel yeh-yeh: gospel's form, without its content, run through the bubblegum gloss of French yé-yé.

Svenonius told the Weekly Wire in 1999: "Our last band, Nation of Ulysses, was a political party. And this one, it's based on gospel." The matching outfits were part of the program. He described the aim as killing off individualism in favor of "a one-ness."

Shows ran on a fixed frame, he said, with an intro, an outro and a middle break: "very vaudevillian in form."

years.cap: Michelle Mae on bass in uniform, Shuffle House, Baltimore, Sept 22, 1996
years.h: The first Make-Up record comes out on the band's own label
years.p: Blue Is Beautiful is the first 7" on Black Gemini. The same year brings Trans-Pleasant Express, a split with [[Slant 6|ffe8acdb-3fa3-4f7e-8939-c3862138502d]], and R.U.A. Believer on K Records.

years.h: Destination: Love; Live! At Cold Rice · Dischord No. 99
years.p: A studio record dressed as a live one, crowd noise included, cut in September 1995 on the Pirate "Mobile" with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]] of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] producing. Dischord calls it Make-Up's debut full-length.
years.xp:
The University of Washington's Online Daily described the live show around these songs as "full of ecstatic screams," with vocals that recalled James Brown and Al Green. Dischord lists 16 tracks, bracketed by an intro and an outro both titled "Hold It."

Dischord remastered it for a 12" LP in 2009.

eras.title: Free Arthur Lee
eras.text: Make-Up worked fast: singles on four labels, the London live album After Dark, and the K Records LP Sound Verite, produced by Calvin Johnson. The politics stayed. The rhythm section got better.

years.cap: James Canty on guitar, Shuffle House, Baltimore, Sept 22, 1996
years.h: Substance Abuse is the second Time Bomb 7"
years.p: It follows We're Having a Baby, released on Time Bomb in 1995.

years.h: A London set becomes After Dark
years.p: Make-Up record a show at Fine China in London in April 1996. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] mixes it at Inner Ear, and it comes out as Dischord No. 105 in February 1997.
years.xp: Dischord lists 13 tracks: a spoken intro, then songs including Blue Is Beautiful and Gospel 2000, closing on a cover of (Here Comes) The Judge.

years.h: Calvin Johnson produces Sound Verite for K
years.p: The LP lands on Olympia's K Records a month after After Dark. Make-Up also turns up on K's Selector Dub Narcotic compilation that year.

years.h: A 7" for Arthur Lee, locked up
years.p: Free Arthur Lee, on K in October 1997, is for the singer of Love, jailed in 1996 after firing a gun during a dispute with a neighbor and on illegal firearms possession. Lee was released in 2001.

years.h: Make-Up cover the spiritual Wade in the Water
years.p: All City Records puts out the traditional song as a single in December 1997.

eras.title: Pow! To the people
eras.text: Royal Trux produced In Mass Mind, Pitchfork put Save Yourself next to the Rolling Stones, and James Schneider turned the band into a thirty-two-minute film.

years.h: Royal Trux produce In Mass Mind, Dischord No. 113
years.p: Make-Up's second Dischord LP has fourteen tracks, cut at Stillness Studio with Neil Hagerty and Jennifer Herrema of [[Royal Trux|87e27246-8c40-407f-bfb3-5dc416557eeb]] producing. The vinyl comes pressed on pink wax.

years.h: James Schneider films Make-Up for Blue Is Beautiful
years.p: Dischord No. 114 is a 32-minute VHS directed by Schneider. It later resurfaces on the In Film/On Video DVD.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the film as a fictionalized tour documentary, with the band playing "cultural refugees" fleeing America and hunted by government agencies. The VHS is out of print.

years.cap: Ian Svenonius at the Empty Bottle, Chicago, Oct 22, 1998
years.h: Two more singles in 1998, and a split with Lungleg
years.p: U R My Intended and Pow! To the People come out on K and Southern. The split 7" is with the Scottish band Lungleg.

years.h: K Records collects the singles on I Want Some
years.p: The scattered 7"s and B-sides land on one album in March 1999.

yt: Live on Spanish TV, Los Conciertos de Radio 3, 1999
years.h: Pitchfork puts Save Yourself beside the Rolling Stones
years.p: Make-Up's last studio album, on K Records. Pitchfork said it could stand next to the Stones' Between the Buttons.
years.xp: Dischord and Black Gemini reissued it on October 4, 2019, on black vinyl and limited plum. The press release called it "a cosmic collision of fuzz and fury."

years.cap: Ian Svenonius at an Edinburgh venue, Nov 19, 1999
years.h: Alex Minoff joins as a fifth member
years.p: The guitarist, later of Golden and [[Extra Golden|c39b100f-0e43-4e39-b244-a33d6dcb09a0]], joins Make-Up for its last months.

eras.title: Out on schedule
eras.text: Make-Up quit in 2000 while the uniforms still fit. Svenonius's stated reason: copycat groups had taken the look and sound and emptied it out.

years.big: "We had a five year plan like Stalin."
years.h: Make-Up end it, right on the five-year plan
years.p: Svenonius on calling it quits. The band's statement blamed copycat groups that had borrowed its look and sound.
years.xp:
He told The Stranger the presentation "was getting redundant because it was getting copied too much," so "we stopped!" Elsewhere: "people were copying us. That's fine. We don't have to do it anymore because they can."

Svenonius, Mae and Alex Minoff formed [[Weird War|f6fb557c-2f0f-4d17-97d9-13371fbe0ea6]] (briefly renamed Scene Creamers) on Drag City. Canty joined [[Ted Leo and the Pharmacists|31095622-5a1e-4f22-8ad1-b08eb6255f37]] and formed French Toast with Jerry Busher.

eras.title: Six years on, the live tapes
eras.text: Six years after the breakup, the live shows got documented properly: the live album Untouchable Sound and the DVD In Film/On Video.

years.h: Untouchable Sound documents the last stretch live
years.p: Drag City and Sea Note release a live Make-Up album from the final months, with Minoff on guitar.

years.h: In Film/On Video puts the Schneider film on DVD
years.p: Dischord No. 156 collects Blue Is Beautiful. Svenonius also publishes The Psychic Soviet, a book of essays, through Drag City.

eras.title: A reunion nobody saw coming
eras.text: For a band that had made quitting part of the concept, a 2012 comeback looked awkward on paper. They played London anyway, then toured again in 2019.

years.cap: Ian Svenonius with Steve Gamboa and Michelle Mae, Alexandra Palace, London, May 27, 2012
years.h: Make-Up's first show since 2000 shares a bill with Slayer
years.p: All Tomorrow's Parties' I'll Be Your Mirror, at London's Alexandra Palace, May 25-27, also has Slayer playing Reign in Blood.
years.xp: Stereogum's post called it a reunion nobody saw coming, and said the band had brought a "'60s-rock shimmy and a refined sense of style" to a Dischord-centric scene. Mogwai and the Afghan Whigs were on the same lineup. At the time there was no word on other dates.

years.h: Dischord presses the debut LP again
years.p: The 2009 remastered vinyl of Destination: Love; Live! At Cold Rice went out of print quickly, so Dischord reissued it in June 2012.

years.cap: Make-Up in matching pink suits, The Bell House, Brooklyn, May 20, 2017
yt: Full set, Zebulon, Los Angeles, Dec 5, 2019
years.h: Make-Up tour again, with Mark Cisneros on drums
years.p: A fall 2019 tour starts October 24 in Philadelphia, timed to the Save Yourself reissue. Cisneros, of [[Des Demonas|7536e54b-aa8f-429a-aa62-21184a53c14c]] and Kid Congo Powers's band, plays drums in place of Gamboa.
years.xp: The first leg ran October 24-31 through Philadelphia, Washington and New York, then December 3-10 from San Diego up to Seattle.
